annotations.keyFindings: Returned referrals fell from 19 to 7 percent and time to triage from 8 to 4 working days after a required-field electronic form in two specialist services.
annotations.limitations: Uncontrolled before-after comparison; a new triage coordinator started in the same month; practice workload not measured.

annotations.keyFindings: In a stepped introduction across 48 practices, time to triage did not differ (adjusted difference 0.3 days); returned referrals fell only where the template was used for most referrals, and 38 percent of referrals bypassed it.
annotations.limitations: Allocation order was random but uptake varied; eight months only; one region.

annotations.keyFindings: Family physicians saw templates as moving work into practices, disliked duplicate fields and bypassed them by attaching letters for complex patients.
annotations.limitations: Volunteer practices; no link to referral outcomes.

annotations.keyFindings: A required test-result field raised urgent referrals with a result from 54 to 91 percent; returned referrals rose for three months and then settled; time to colonoscopy did not change.
annotations.limitations: One region; practices without rapid kits returned most referrals.

annotations.keyFindings: About 60 percent of triage nurse time was rework; a redesign with a returned-referral queue and fixed triage time cut lead time from 12 to 6 working days without a template.
annotations.limitations: Before-after comparison without control; four months of follow-up.

annotations.keyFindings: Thirteen of 21 studies reported more complete referrals with structured forms; effects on waiting times were inconsistent (three shorter, four no change) and practice time was rarely measured.
annotations.limitations: Mostly uncontrolled studies; varied definitions of referral quality.

claims.text: After a required-field electronic referral form, returned referrals fell from 19 to 7 percent and the median time to triage from 8 to 4 working days.
claims.passage: Referrals returned to family practices for missing information fell from 19 percent to 7 percent, and the median time from receipt to a triage decision fell from 8 to 4 working days.
claims.interpretation: A large before-after effect, confounded by a new coordinator.

claims.text: In a stepped introduction across 48 practices, a mandatory-field template did not change the time to triage, and 38 percent of referrals bypassed the required fields.
claims.passage: Overall, 38 percent of referrals bypassed the required fields by attaching a free-text letter.
claims.interpretation: The best-controlled study finds no effect on triage time and widespread bypass.

claims.text: Whether a structured referral template shortens the time to triage is uncertain: an uncontrolled before-after study reported a halving, while a stepped introduction across 48 practices found no difference.
claims.passage: there was no difference in the time from receipt to triage decision between periods with and without the template
claims.interpretation: The evidence conflicts on the outcome the intake cares most about; the local redesign must measure it rather than assume it.

claims.text: Family physicians described structured templates as moving the specialist service's work into practices and bypassed required fields by attaching letters.
claims.passage: Many described the templates as moving the specialist service's work into the practice without extra time.
claims.interpretation: Practice workload and bypass are balancing measures, not side notes.

claims.text: A required test-result field raised urgent lower gastrointestinal referrals with a result from 54 to 91 percent, while returned referrals rose for about three months.
claims.passage: the proportion of urgent referrals with a test result rose from 54 percent to 91 percent
claims.interpretation: Required fields improve completeness but create a transition cost for practices without rapid test kits.

synthesis: Six retrieved records from a second, broader search, appraised at abstract level; the first, narrow search for this intake's own question returned nothing and was confirmed empty by the investigator. Structured forms make referrals more complete (a review of 21 studies and a gastroenterology time series), but effects on access conflict: an uncontrolled before-after study reported triage time halving, while the best-controlled study, a stepped introduction across 48 practices, found no difference and widespread bypass of required fields. Family physicians describe templates as moving work into practices, and practices without rapid test kits return the most referrals. A value stream study shows that most triage nurse time is rework and that process redesign alone halved lead time. The body of evidence answers different questions with different designs, and no single certainty rating would be meaningful across completeness, triage time and practice workload.
gradeRationale: Not assessed as one rating: completeness, triage time and practice workload are separate outcomes, the only controlled study conflicts with the uncontrolled ones on triage time, and practice workload is barely measured. Per-record grades are given; overall certainty is left unassessed.
summary: Six retrieved records appraised; five claims recorded, one an inference with high uncertainty about conflicting results; overall certainty deliberately not assessed.
